title: The cache that served another tenant
blurb: A prefix-only key leaked completions across tenants.
prompt: A tenant noticed completions referencing a product they do not use; the cache key omitted the tenant, so the first tenant to warm a popular prefix served everyone. The same cache refreshed TTLs on hit so a deprecated version never expired. Review it, fix it, and prove keys are tenant- and version-scoped.
aiNote: The draft builds the cache key from the prefix hash alone and refreshes the value's TTL on every hit, so entries cross tenant boundaries and a hot deprecated version effectively never expires.
testIdea: Warm a prefix as tenant A, request it as tenant B and assert a miss; bump the prompt version and assert the old namespace stops serving; assert a hot entry still reports the original TTL rather than an extended one.
followUps: When is a cached completion still safe to serve after a model update?
What should happen to the cache when a prompt version is rolled back?
How would you price the savings number so finance trusts it?
